description: Single-player Yahtzee TUI built with Python Textual — ASCII-art dice, keyboard-only navigation, all 13 official scoring categories, live score preview, dark terminal theme.

userStories.title: Implement scoring logic as a pure-function module
userStories.description: As a developer, I want all 13 Yahtzee scoring rules implemented as pure functions so that scoring is correct, independently testable, and has no Textual dependency.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a module (e.g. scoring.py) with one function per category: ones, twos, threes, fours, fives, sixes, three_of_a_kind, four_of_a_kind, full_house, small_straight, large_straight, yahtzee, chance
Each function accepts a list of 5 integers (die values 1–6) and returns an integer score
Ones–Sixes: return sum of dice matching that face value
Three of a Kind: return sum of all 5 dice if any value appears ≥3 times, else 0
Four of a Kind: return sum of all 5 dice if any value appears ≥4 times, else 0
Full House: return 25 if dice contain exactly three of one value and two of another, else 0
Small Straight: return 30 if dice contain any 4 sequential values (1-2-3-4, 2-3-4-5, or 3-4-5-6), else 0
Large Straight: return 40 if dice are exactly 1-2-3-4-5 or 2-3-4-5-6, else 0
Yahtzee: return 50 if all 5 dice show the same value, else 0
Chance: return sum of all 5 dice, always
Unit tests cover all 13 functions, including edge cases (e.g. empty straights, boundary counts)
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Implemented scoring.py with 13 pure functions; 55 unit tests all passing.

userStories.title: Implement game state model
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a game state class or dataclass that tracks all mutable game data so that the Textual UI can read and mutate state without mixing logic into widgets.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a GameState class (e.g. in game.py) with attributes: dice (list of 5 ints, default 0 = unrolled), held (list of 5 bools), roll_count (int 0–3), scores (dict mapping category name to int or None), game_over (bool)
Provide a roll() method that randomizes unheld dice and increments roll_count; raises or no-ops if roll_count >= 3
Provide a toggle_hold(index) method that flips held[index]; only callable when roll_count >= 1
Provide a commit(category) method that stores the current score for the given category and resets dice, held, and roll_count for the next turn; raises if category already committed or roll_count == 0
Provide a reset() method that returns all state to initial values
Provide an upper_subtotal property returning the sum of committed Ones–Sixes scores
Provide a bonus property returning 35 if upper_subtotal >= 63, else 0
Provide a grand_total property returning sum of all committed scores plus bonus
Provide a is_game_over property returning True when all 13 categories are committed
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Implemented game.py with GameState class; 43 unit tests all passing.

userStories.title: Scaffold the Textual app with two-panel layout and dark theme
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the Textual App class and TCSS stylesheet in place with a two-panel layout (dice panel left, scorecard panel right) and a dark color theme so that all subsequent widgets have a home.
acceptanceCriteria: Create main app entry point (e.g. main.py or yahtzee/app.py) subclassing textual.app.App
Layout is a two-column horizontal split: left panel for dice area, right panel for scorecard
A header bar shows the game title 'YAHTZEE' and the roll counter placeholder
A TCSS file (app.tcss) controls all colors; no inline styles in Python code
Background is dark (e.g. #1a1a2e or similar dark terminal color); all text is light-on-dark
No mouse bindings are registered anywhere (ALLOW_IN_MAXIMIZED_VIEW or on_mouse_* handlers must not exist)
Running the app with 'python -m yahtzee' (or equivalent) opens the TUI without errors
Verify visually by running the app in a terminal
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Created yahtzee/ package with App subclass, two-panel horizontal layout, Header showing YAHTZEE title and Roll 0/3 subtitle, all styles in app.tcss (dark #1a1a2e background), no mouse handlers. Runnable via python -m yahtzee.

userStories.title: Render five dice as ASCII art widgets
userStories.description: As a player, I want to see five dice drawn in ASCII art so that the game feels tactile and readable in the terminal.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a DieWidget custom Textual widget that renders one die as a 5-row ASCII box with pip characters
Pip layouts match standard die conventions: 1=center, 2=top-right/bottom-left, 3=diagonal+center, 4=corners, 5=corners+center, 6=two columns of three
Five DieWidget instances are displayed in a horizontal row in the left panel
An unheld, unfocused die uses a plain dim border
A held die shows a distinct border style (e.g. double or bright) and a 'HELD' label below the box
The focused die shows an accent-colored highlighted border
A die that is both held and focused shows both indicators simultaneously
Dice with value 0 (unrolled state) display an empty or blank face
Verify visually by running the app in a terminal
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Created yahtzee/die_widget.py with DieWidget (can_focus=True); pip layouts for faces 0-6; held/focus border states via CSS; HELD label via reactive watch_held. Five DieWidget instances in a Horizontal #dice-row inside #dice-panel. All 98 tests still pass.

userStories.title: Implement roll action and hold/release toggle
userStories.description: As a player, I want to roll the dice and hold specific ones so that I can pursue scoring combinations across up to three rolls per turn.
acceptanceCriteria: Pressing 'r' (or 'R') anywhere in the app calls GameState.roll() and refreshes all five DieWidget displays
On the first roll, all five dice receive new random values (1–6)
On the 2nd and 3rd roll, only unheld dice are re-randomized; held dice keep their values
The roll counter in the header updates to 'Roll 1/3', 'Roll 2/3', 'Roll 3/3' after each roll
After 3 rolls, pressing 'r' has no effect
Pressing Space while a DieWidget is focused calls GameState.toggle_hold(index) and refreshes that die's display
Holding is only actionable when roll_count >= 1 (Space has no effect before the first roll)
All dice start each turn (after a commit or reset) as unheld
Verify visually by running the app in a terminal
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Wired GameState into YahtzeeApp (on_mount); 'r' binding calls action_roll() which updates all DieWidget values and sub_title; DieWidget posts ToggleHoldRequest on Space; App handler calls game.toggle_hold() and refreshes die.held. All 98 tests still pass.

userStories.title: Keyboard navigation between the five dice
userStories.description: As a player, I want to navigate between the five dice with Left/Right arrow keys and switch to the scorecard with Tab so that I never need a mouse.
acceptanceCriteria: Left/Right arrow keys move focus between the five DieWidget instances when the dice panel is active
Focus wraps: pressing Right on die 5 moves focus to die 1, pressing Left on die 1 moves focus to die 5
The newly focused die is visually highlighted (accent border)
Pressing Tab while any die is focused moves focus to the scorecard panel
No mouse event handlers are used for focus management
Verify visually by running the app in a terminal
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Added left/right bindings to DieWidget with modulo-wrap navigation; tab binding delegates to action_focus_scorecard() which queries first focusable in #scorecard-panel (no-op until US-007 adds content). All 98 tests still pass.

userStories.title: Display the scorecard with all 13 categories and totals
userStories.description: As a player, I want to see all 13 scoring categories in a scorecard panel with upper/lower sections and running totals so that I know what I can score and what I have already committed.
acceptanceCriteria: The right panel shows a ScorecardWidget listing all 13 categories in two labelled sections: UPPER SECTION (Ones, Twos, Threes, Fours, Fives, Sixes) and LOWER SECTION (Three of a Kind, Four of a Kind, Full House, Small Straight, Large Straight, Yahtzee, Chance)
Each row shows: category name, and a score column (blank if uncommitted, committed value if committed)

Between sections: a subtotal row showing the current upper section sum (e.g. 'Subtotal: 9 / 63'), a bonus row ('+35 BONUS' or '—'), and a 'Need X more for bonus' hint while upper section is incomplete
A TOTAL row at the bottom shows the current grand total
Committed categories are visually dimmed or styled differently from available ones
Scorecard reads from GameState (scores, upper_subtotal, bonus, grand_total properties)
Verify visually by running the app in a terminal
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Show live score preview for available categories after each roll
userStories.description: As a player, I want to see what each available category would score with my current dice after every roll, so that I can make informed decisions before committing.
acceptanceCriteria: After every roll, the ScorecardWidget calls the relevant scoring function for each uncommitted category and displays the result as a preview score in a muted/italic style
Preview scores are visually distinct from committed scores (e.g. different color, enclosed in brackets, or italicised)
A category that would score 0 shows '0' as the preview, not blank
Preview scores update automatically on every roll without manual refresh
Before the first roll of a turn (roll_count == 0), no preview is shown for any category
Once a category is committed, its preview disappears and the committed value is shown permanently
Verify visually by running the app in a terminal
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Keyboard navigation within the scorecard
userStories.description: As a player, I want to navigate scoring categories with Up/Down arrow keys and return to the dice area with Tab so that I can select a category to commit without using a mouse.
acceptanceCriteria: Up/Down arrow keys move focus between available (uncommitted) category rows in the ScorecardWidget when the scorecard panel is active
Already-committed categories are skipped — focus never lands on them
The focused category row is clearly highlighted (e.g. inverted colors or accent background)
Pressing Tab while the scorecard is active moves focus back to the dice panel (landing on the last or first focused die)
No mouse event handlers are used for scorecard navigation
Verify visually by running the app in a terminal
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Commit a score to a category and end the turn
userStories.description: As a player, I want to press Enter on a focused scorecard category to commit my dice score and end the turn so that my progress is recorded and the next turn begins.
acceptanceCriteria: Pressing Enter while a scorecard category is focused calls GameState.commit(category) with the current dice
Committing is only possible after at least one roll (roll_count >= 1); Enter has no effect otherwise
After committing, the turn resets: all dice show blank faces, all held states clear, roll_count resets to 0
The committed score is permanently displayed in the scorecard row and the category is marked as used (dimmed)
The scorecard subtotal, bonus, grand total, and 'needed for bonus' indicator all update immediately after commit
Verify visually by running the app in a terminal
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Detect end of game and show final score screen
userStories.description: As a player, I want the game to end and display my final score after all 13 categories are committed so that I know my result and can choose to play again.
acceptanceCriteria: After each commit, GameState.is_game_over is checked
When all 13 categories are committed, an end-game overlay or screen is shown on top of the TUI
The end-game screen displays the final grand total (sum of all 13 committed scores plus bonus if earned)
The end-game screen shows whether the upper section bonus was earned
The end-game screen prompts: 'Press N to play again'
While the end-game screen is visible, the dice area, roll shortcut (R), and commit action (Enter on scorecard) are all disabled
Verify visually by running the app in a terminal
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Start a new game with the N key
userStories.description: As a player, I want to press N to start a new game so that I can play again without restarting the application.
acceptanceCriteria: Pressing 'n' (or 'N') at any time calls GameState.reset() and refreshes the entire UI
After reset: all 13 scorecard categories are blank, all dice show blank faces, roll counter shows 'Roll 0/3', focus returns to the first die
If N is pressed mid-game (at least one category already committed and game is not over), a confirmation dialog is shown: 'Start a new game? (Y to confirm, any other key to cancel)'
If the player confirms (presses Y), the game resets; any other key dismisses the dialog without resetting
If N is pressed from the end-game screen, no confirmation is needed — the game resets immediately
If N is pressed before any category is committed, no confirmation is needed
Verify visually by running the app in a terminal
Typecheck passes
